title: Needs for finance and matching their duration

blocks.heading: Needs for finance and matching their duration
blocks.text: A need for finance states why money is required; a source states where it comes from. Businesses need funds to start operations, buy or replace equipment, expand and pay operating expenses before customer receipts arrive. A new machine is an investment need, while wages and materials can create a working-capital need. Long-lived assets are normally better matched to longer-term finance so that repayment does not fall due before the asset generates sufficient receipts. A temporary cash gap may suit an agreed overdraft or supplier credit if its duration and cost fit. Short-term finance is not automatically cheaper or available. Long-term borrowing commits the firm to repayments and interest; equity avoids scheduled loan repayments but shares ownership and potential returns. Match amount, purpose, duration, affordability and risk. A profitable business can still need finance because sales revenue may not yet have been collected. Conversely, borrowing provides cash but is not profit from trading.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nera Bricks needs a kiln expected to last several years and materials to fill a confirmed order whose customer pays after delivery. The kiln is a long-term asset need; materials create a shorter operating gap. A medium- or long-term loan may match the kiln, while supplier credit could help the materials timing if agreed terms fit the expected receipts. The word loan names a source, not the reason money is needed.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why “bank loan” does not identify Nalu Bakery’s need for finance. Nalu needs money to replace its broken oven and is considering borrowing.

Replacing the oven is the need: it states the intended use of the money. A bank loan is a possible source: it states where the money would come from and how it would be financed. The same oven need could be met from retained cash, if available, so the purpose and source cannot be substituted for one another.
